terminal.module.css (new): full CSS Module with --accent #2EE6F6, --backdrop #0BD3E6, --prompt #5BE6A0 tokens; page container with container-type:inline-size/container-name:page; window min(980px,100%) x min(84vh,780px), exact 3-layer shadow, radius 13px; title bar with traffic-light dots; scrollable body with clamp padding and scrollbar styles; wordmark clamp(28px,7cqw,46px) weight 800; specialities grid; status bar; @container page (max-width:560px) breakpoint collapsing grid to 1 column, window full-height/radius 14px, hiding zsh and brand label, shrinking status bar

terminal.tsx rewritten as use client component: static intro (prompt, wordmark, subtitle, value-prop, // specialities comment + 4-item grid, tip, divider, input row, status bar); controlled input with useState; auto-focus via useEffect 650ms; click-to-refocus on body; 18 lines in status bar; faint dot grid as fixed aria-hidden div
left_undone: Click-to-refocus behaviour after commands and auto-scroll (depends on feed — later feature)
AI streaming integration and deferred CAPTCHA flow (later feature)
Removal of chat-terminal.tsx, code-block.tsx, captcha-overlay.tsx (later cleanup feature)
issues_discovered: The faint dot grid is implemented as a fixed aria-hidden <div> inside the page container (matching the reference HTML structure) rather than body::before, which would create its own stacking context and paint over the window.
Scrollbar styles must live in the CSS Module (scoped .body class), not globals.css, because CSS Module class names are compile-time scoped and unreachable from globals.
A literal // specialities text node in JSX trips react/jsx-no-comment-textnodes; wrap it in a string expression {'// specialities'}.
JetBrains_Mono with weight 400/500/700/800 x normal/italic loads 8 font files; only italic 400 is used, so italic 500/700/800 are loaded but unused — candidate for a small cleanup.
procedures_followed: risky-scan clean (ok) before staging and after

decisions.situation: Reference HTML container query sets the mobile window border-radius to 14px, while the narrow-screen criterion describes a 'smaller' radius than the 13px base; the two conflict.
decisions.action: Followed the reference HTML literally (14px under 560px) because the handoff README names the reference HTML as the source of truth for exact values; the discrepancy is noted so review judges against the reference.
